# Forensic Dossier — Logista (LOG.MC) | Industrials / Distribution | Signal: deep_value

*Source material: four consecutive results calls (H1-2024, FY-2024, H1-2025, FY-2025) cross-referenced against the screener's multi-year financial trajectory and the TTM/latest-quarter overrides.*

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Logista's story across these four calls is the slow, managed substitution of one earnings engine for another — and the quiet discovery that the replacement engine is worse than advertised.

**The opening frame (H1-2024).** Management leads with "a solid set of results, thanks to the growth of different business lines, **the profit on inventory** recorded for the period and **the evolution of the interest rates**" (H1-2024). Both load-bearing tailwinds are named in the first breath: profit-on-inventory (POI) from tobacco price/tax moves, and financial income on the ~€2bn Imperial Brands cash float. The structural story is *diversification away from tobacco* — "maintaining the ratio of non-tobacco related economic sales higher than 50%" — executed via bolt-on M&A (SGEL Libros, Belgium Parcels Service, El Mosca, Speedlink). The February 2024 credit-line addendum to "partially hedge the potential interest rate risk for the next 3 years" is presented as prudent foresight; in hindsight it is management bracing for the financial-income engine to roll over.

**The mid-arc (FY-2024).** Confidence peaks. Net profit €308m (+13%), dividend raised 30% to €2.09/share, financial income €93m "thanks to the higher average interest rate." Diversification is celebrated — 100% ownership consummated across El Mosca/Speedlink, "6 transactions… surpass the 50% threshold." But the first stress crack is audible: long-haul transport is "tightening," Red Sea disruption, "excess capacity in the market." Management is still offensive, talking M&A pipeline ("similar size to El Mosca, why not").

**The pivot (H1-2025 → FY-2025).** The narrative inverts. The *diversification asset* becomes the *problem child*. By H1-2025, El Mosca and the Carbó frozen business "has suffered from macroeconomic situation… lower European demand," and management is no longer pitching growth — it is itemizing a turnaround: "new management," "logistics control measures and compliance procedures," "optimizing the client mix," route integration with Logista Freight. By FY-2025, the language is fully defensive: El Mosca "has had a challenging year," "sluggish demand across Europe and margin compression," Carbó suffered "increasing competition, which has led to the loss of clients against competitors." Simultaneously the financial-income engine is in visible decline — €103m (FY24) → €73m (FY25) as the ECB rate fell from 4.85% to 3.54% average. The dividend, once *raised*, is now *defended*: FY-2025 holds it flat at €277m via a **99% payout ratio**, explicitly "despite the need to increase the payout ratio."

**Growth drivers introduced then muted.** The "big/transformational acquisition in Europe in 2025" floated at FY-2024 is walked back by H1-2025 ("the number big or transformational is not part of our aim") and by FY-2025 reframed as "put on hold a couple of opportunities" while management restructures El Mosca. The recycle-NGP initiative, hyped early, is conceded to be "around 1% to 2% of the EBIT coming from Italy" — immaterial. Net: the bull drivers (diversification growth, transformational M&A, new revenue lines) have all been trimmed; the two engines that actually move the P&L (POI, financial income) are the two management least controls.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Quarter | The actual numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Solid set of results… growth of different business lines" | every call | Revenue 12.43B→12.99B→13.54B (+4.2% YoY, 3-yr CAGR +5.7%); economic sales +3–4%. Top line is genuinely, if slowly, growing. | **Matches** — modest, real top-line growth |
| Net profit strength / dividend coverage | H1-24, FY-24 | NI 2023 €272m → 2024 €308m (+13%), then **2025 €281m (−9%)**. EPS 2.07→2.34→**2.13 (−9% YoY)**. The peak was FY-24; FY-25 gave back the gain. | **Diverges** — earnings *peaked and rolled*; the "solid" framing masks a down year |
| Financial income is a durable contributor | H1-24 ("evolution of interest rates") | €53m (H1-24) → €93m (FY-24) → €73m (FY-25), and falling as ECB cuts. ~50% hedged at ~3.6%; the unhedged ~€1bn float re-prices down with Euribor. | **Diverges** — explicitly a *melting* tailwind; management's own hedge admits it |
| POI is a recurring earnings lever | FY-25 ("third consecutive year… substantial POI") | €25m (H1-24) → €35m (FY-24) → **€45m (FY-25)**. Real and rising — *but* management repeatedly warns it is "not under our control… the manufacturers… deciding when and how they increase prices." | **Partially matches** — real cash, but low-quality (exogenous, tobacco-tax-dependent, one-off in character) |
| Diversification de-risks the business | every call | The diversified assets (El Mosca long-haul, Carbó frozen) are precisely what *broke* in 2025, importing cyclical European-freight risk the legacy tobacco book never had. ROE 41.3% / ROIC 19.6% are still elite — but driven by asset-light tobacco + the cash float, not the new cyclical legs. | **Diverges** — diversification *added* cyclicality and a turnaround liability rather than removing risk |
| FCF / cash-generation quality | screener | Scan shows P/FCF 7.3x and FCF +58.9% YoY — but the **TTM FCF override is just €66m** vs ~€280m net income. FCF conversion has collapsed (working-capital swings in tobacco distribution + transport capex). | **Diverges sharply** — the headline "7.3x FCF / value" screen is contradicted by €66m TTM FCF; the cheap-on-FCF thesis is fragile |
| Balance sheet | screener override | Scan net debt €733m is **wrong**; live recompute = **€184m net debt, effectively near net-cash** given the €2bn Imperial float sits against it. Altman-Z 3.1 (safe), Piotroski 6/9. | **Green** — balance sheet is sound; the headline-debt scare is a data artifact |

**Synthesis of the forensic read:** The valuation models violently disagree for a *structural* reason. Buffett/EPV-style FV (€22.8; EPV margin-of-safety **−100%**) treats Logista as a low-margin (net 2.1%, gross 3.6%) distributor whose *normalized* earnings power — stripped of POI windfalls and a peak-rate cash float — is thin and shrinking. DCF FV (€64.3, +49%) capitalizes the *current* elevated cash flows (POI + financial income at recent highs) as if durable. The truth sits between: at €33 the stock is **not cheap on normalized earnings power** but **is supported by a fat, well-covered (until now) dividend and a near-net-cash balance sheet**. The deep_value tag is only valid if you believe POI keeps recurring and rates don't fully normalize away the float income — both of which management itself flags as outside its control.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Trajectory: DECLINING (offensive → defensive over four calls).**

- **H1-2024 — Confident/offensive.** "Solid set of results"; active M&A ("we continue to seek new transactions"); growth-line emphasis. Caveats are external (Red Sea, weather). *Specificity: high on tailwinds, vague on the float roll-off.*
- **FY-2024 — Peak confidence.** Dividend +30%; "transformational… why not"; "relatively more positive for '25." This is the high-water mark of the narrative.
- **H1-2025 — Turning defensive.** Opens by flagging El Mosca/Carbó weakness; introduces turnaround vocabulary ("new management," "compliance procedures," "optimize the client mix"). Net profit −5%, blamed on "lower interest rates." Still claims "EBIT in line with market expectations" but hedges heavily ("too soon," "not under our control").
- **FY-2025 — Fully defensive.** "Challenging year," "sluggish demand," "margin compression," "loss of clients against competitors." Dividend now *defended* not grown, via 99% payout. M&A reframed from offense to "put on hold… focused on integration and restructuring." Explicit admission of caution: on whether El Mosca makes them more cautious on acquisitions, "The fair answer is to say, yes."

The arc is a clean, monotonic slide from growth/investment language to efficiency/cost/restructuring language — the classic late-cycle distributor signature.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Logista guides loosely and on purpose — "adjusted EBIT mid-single-digit growth **excluding** profit on inventory" is the only hard frame, and it is deliberately POI-agnostic because POI "is not under our control."

- **On the ex-POI EBIT guide:** *Delivered.* H1-2024 "fully aligned with our guidance of mid-single digit excluding inventory revaluation reaching 5%." Reliable on the metric they can steer.
- **On POI itself:** They refuse to forecast it ("It's quite difficult to foresee the exact number," H1-2024) and proved right to — POI has been volatile (€25m/€35m/€45m). Honest about uncertainty, but it means the *most material* swing factor is un-guided.
- **On the dividend:** Promised "at least the same dividend as 2024" and delivered it — but only by pushing the payout to **99%**, which the FY-24 framing ("at least 90% of net profit") did not telegraph. The commitment held; the *quality* of how it held (no longer covered with a buffer) is a downgrade.
- **On the "transformational M&A" floated FY-2024:** *Missed / quietly retracted.* By FY-2025 it is "on hold." Analysts (Jorge Orte) called this out directly: "In November, Logista said it was considering a big acquisition… Why is that being delayed?" Management's walk-back ("more than a delay… we put on hold") is a soft miss.

**Earnings-delivery context:** EPS 3-yr CAGR +12.2%, but the *latest* prints are deteriorating — FY EPS −9%, consensus forward EPS growth +0.5% (i.e. the street already models a flat-to-stalling year). Note the override: **latest-Q EPS YoY +84% and TTM diluted EPS 3.02** — a sharp positive quarterly inflection that sits *against* the −9% fiscal-year read, likely POI/seasonality-driven and not yet proven durable.

**Reliability score: MEDIUM.** They hit what they steer (ex-POI EBIT, the dividend), are candid about what they can't (POI), but over-promised on transformational M&A and let dividend coverage quietly erode to defend the headline payout.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Recurring pressure clusters, and where they led:

1. **"Will the dividend survive falling profit?"** (Kepler, FY-24: "in the case that net profit drops in 2025 due to lower POI and financial income, do you intend to increase your payout ratio?"). Management initially gave reassurance about "the Board… completely aligned"; the bad-news payoff arrived FY-25 as the **99% payout** — exactly the forced payout-ratio expansion analysts feared.
2. **El Mosca / long-haul deterioration.** Pressed every call from H1-2024 onward. Management's answers degraded from "too premature" (H1-24) to a full restructuring confession (FY-25). Analysts smelled this early; management was slow to concede the scale.
3. **POI normalization** ("reasonable level of POI for the year," BNP, repeatedly). Persistent deflection ("difficult to foresee," "not under our control") — legitimate, but it leaves the single biggest earnings driver permanently un-modelable, a real risk the market under-weights.
4. **Financial-income cliff.** Analysts repeatedly probed the net-financial-income run-rate at current Euribor (Francisco Ruiz, H1-25: "best estimate for net financial income… at current Euribor?"). Management gave ~€65–70m — i.e. *guided the tailwind down* in real time. The market that bid the stock to 81% of its 52-wk range may be slow to price this melt.
5. **"Transformational M&A — where is it?"** Pushed by multiple desks; answered with retraction. The growth optionality analysts were underwriting has been removed.

The through-line: analysts have been *correctly* worried about (a) dividend coverage, (b) the cyclical transport drag, and (c) the dual fade of POI + float income. Management has been candid-but-late on each.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **Red flags**
- 🔴 **Earnings rolled over (FY-25 NI −9%, EPS −9%)** after peaking FY-24 — the diversification story did not prevent a down year; it caused part of it.
- 🔴 **99% dividend payout** to hold the headline DPS flat — coverage buffer gone; any further POI/financial-income fade forces a real cut.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **M&A posture reversal:** from "transformational… why not" (FY-24) to "more cautious… the fair answer is yes" (FY-25), explicitly because El Mosca burned them. The acquisition machine — a core part of the bull story — has been throttled by its own integration failure.
- **"One-off costs that will not roll over to '26"** (FY-25) — management pre-committing that restructuring charges are ring-fenced. This is a forward-looking promise to watch; if 2026 carries *more* El Mosca/Carbó charges, credibility takes a real hit.
- **Two CFO/CEO voices, consistent message:** Losada (CFO) and Meirás/Amusco (CEO) hand off cleanly; no internal narrative dissonance — but also no fresh strategic voice introducing a new growth vector. The bench is steady but the playbook is unchanged.
- **Tobacco-tax dependency is now the de-facto earnings strategy:** three straight years of POI from tax-driven price hikes have become a structural assumption, even as management disclaims control. The business increasingly *needs* governments to keep raising tobacco taxes — an odd, fragile dependency for a "defensive" name.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: PIVOTING (tilting toward DETERIORATING on the engines that matter).**

Logista is mid-pivot: a cash-rich, high-ROIC tobacco-distribution franchise deliberately rotating into logistics/pharma/courier to outlast secular tobacco decline — but the rotation has, so far, *imported* cyclical risk (El Mosca, Carbó) faster than it has built durable new earnings power, while the two tailwinds that flattered 2023–2024 (POI windfalls and a peak-rate cash float) are both fading or un-guidable. Earnings peaked in FY-2024 and rolled −9% in FY-2025; the dividend is now defended at a 99% payout rather than grown.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** *the durability of the dividend and of "normalized" earnings power once the rate-float income and POI windfalls normalize.* The entire deep_value case rests on whether €33 is buying a stable ~6% yielder with a near-net-cash balance sheet and a slowly-compounding diversified base (DCF view, FV €64) — or a melting tobacco annuity whose headline cheapness is propped by un-repeatable POI and a fading interest-rate tailwind, with a payout one bad year from a cut (Buffett/EPV view, FV €22.8, EPV MoS −100%). There is no hard catalyst here — no buyback authorization, no activist, no asset sale, no spin — only a fat dividend and a cyclical-transport self-help turnaround. Size it as a yield/quality-value position with explicit POI- and rate-sensitivity haircuts, not as an event-driven value re-rating.
